subject.title: [Feature]: Expose before_tool_call/after_tool_call in internal hooks system

question: Should managed internal HOOK.md hooks be allowed to synchronously block or rewrite tool calls, or should tool-call enforcement remain limited to typed plugin hooks?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix changes a security-sensitive tool execution boundary and could create a second policy API with different semantics from plugin hooks.

options.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
options.body: Add a typed internal before/after tool-call contract only after defining timeout, failure, block, rewrite, audit, and docs/test requirements.

options.title: Keep policy plugin-only
options.body: Close or narrow this issue after documenting that HOOK.md hooks are for operator automation while typed plugin hooks own runtime policy decisions.

options.title: Expose observe-only internal events
options.body: Allow after-tool or telemetry-style HOOK.md events while leaving pre-execution blocking and parameter rewriting in plugin hooks.

recommendation.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
recommendation.body: Add a typed internal before/after tool-call contract only after defining timeout, failure, block, rewrite, audit, and docs/test requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on internal hooks plus an explicit discussion signal keeping this as the canonical tracker.
